From: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@finpay.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment pen test artifact request & boundary clarification

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our InfoSec team has one follow-up related to the penetration test artifacts for the private (customer VPC) deployment we're piloting. They have three asks we need to resolve before we can sign off:

1) A diagram or short narrative that explicitly states what lives inside our VPC vs what runs in Redwood-managed infrastructure. In particular: where does the KV cache live, where are GPU instances hosted, and whether any control-plane components ever touch plaintext customer data.

2) A copy of the most recent penetration test summary for Private Deployments (redacted is fine), plus the current remediation status for any medium/high findings that relate to network boundary or SSH exposure.

3) Proof of the network changes you made after the last test — e.g. ACL snapshots, security group rules, or a short audit log showing rule changes.

I attached our compliance checklist (finpay-pt-checklist.xlsx). Could you loop in the engineer who can provide the ACL snapshots and a brief segmentation matrix? Nico from our contractor (RedTeam Assess) is CC'd; they may request additional evidence.

We'd like to close this by EOD Friday (2026-11-13) if possible.

Regards,
Sarah Miller
Head of InfoSec, FinPay Inc.
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@finpay.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Nico Alvarez <n.alvarez@redteam-assess.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment pen test artifact request & boundary clarification

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear checklist.

Quick answers up front:
- Customer VPC (your VPC) contains the customer-controlled subnets, NAT, and the private ENIs for model inference. GPU instances for the private deployment are launched in the customer VPC under an auto-scaling group we provision; logs and metrics are shipped to a customer-owned logging bucket if you enable that option.
- The Redwood control plane (for orchestration/metrics) runs in Redwood-managed accounts and never receives plaintext customer payloads. We use mutual TLS and encrypted channels; keys never leave your KMS when configured for private deployments.
- KV cache for short-term inference caching is optional: when enabled in Private mode, it is deployed as a managed service inside the customer VPC (hosted as a container backed by a customer-owned subnet) — the default config keeps the cache inside your network boundary.

I'm attaching our redacted summary of the private deployment PT we ran earlier this year (priv-deploy-pt-summary-redacted.pdf). Mina is copied — she'll provide the segmentation matrix and the ACL snapshots you requested.

If you want, we can do a 30 min sync with your team + Nico tomorrow morning to walk through the artifacts.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
pri_yom@redwood.ai
Attachments: priv-deploy-pt-summary-redacted.pdf (pdf)

Subject: Re: Private deployment pen test artifact request & boundary clarification

Hi Sarah — following up with the technical evidence you requested.

I've attached two artifacts: a vpc-segmentation-matrix.csv that maps each functional component to the VPC/subnet and ownership (customer vs Redwood-managed), and egress-acls.txt which are the text exports of the security group / NACL rules before/after remediation for the one medium finding in the prior test.

High-level notes (summary of changes):
- Finding: In the original test, a staging GPU instance had an overly permissive SSH rule that allowed 0.0.0.0/0 on TCP/22 for a short diagnostic window.
- Remediation: We replaced the SG with a new SG limiting SSH to the customer's bastion host CIDR (10.12.7.0/27) and disabled direct public IP assignment for GPU instances. We also enforced host-based firewall rules (ufw/iptables) via our bootstrap script.
- KV cache boundary: the managed cache lives inside your private subnet (10.12.0.0/16) and is reachable only via the model-inference subnet; no outbound rules permit 0.0.0.0/0 egress from the cache.
- Control-plane traffic: only metrics/health checks are proxied over mTLS to Redwood endpoints; payloads are encrypted in transit and at rest per our SOC 2 controls mapping (see column D in the attached matrix).

Attached: vpc-segmentation-matrix.csv (csv), egress-acls.txt (text)

If you need timestamped ACL snapshots for audit, I can pull the historic security-group change logs (we have CloudTrail events for the rule-change at 2026-11-09T22:14:35Z). I added the remediation status for each finding in the CSV; the medium SSH exposure is marked 'closed' and references JIRA SUP-4982 (our internal ticket).

Would you prefer the artifacts uploaded to your S3 bucket or shared via the secure Drive link (I can put them behind a signed URL)?

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: vpc-segmentation-matrix.csv, egress-acls.txt

Thanks Mina — this is helpful. Quick follow-ups:

1) Can you share the CloudTrail event ID or a screenshot of the security-group change that closed the SSH finding? Nico will want to cross-reference.
2) For the KV cache, can you confirm the exact subnet IDs and whether the cache service uses a managed ENI that could be reassigned across instances? We need to validate that the cache cannot be egress-proxied to Redwood-managed networks.

Also — in the CSV I noticed one item mapped as 'customer-managed logging bucket optional' — we will enable that, but can you note how logs are redacted or filtered (PII filter) before any metrics leave our VPC?

If possible, drop the artifacts into our S3 path (s3://finpay-compliance/proof/) with a signed URL and provide the CloudTrail event reference. If not, the secure Drive link works.

Sarah

Hi Sarah — quick status update and links to the artifacts per your request.

1) CloudTrail reference: change event id arn:aws:cloudtrail:us-west-2:123456789012:event/0a1b2c3d-4e5f-6789-abcd-0123456789ab (timestamp 2026-11-09T22:14:35Z). The event shows the sg-0a1b2c3d replaced with sg-7f8e9d0c and the description in the event is 'restrict-ssh-to-bastion'.

2) KV cache details: subnet IDs where cache is deployed: subnet-0a12b34c (private-inference-1), subnet-0b23c45d (private-inference-2). The cache uses an ENI within those subnets and is created with attribute 'assignPublicIp=false'. The cache process is pinned to the VPC-local CIDR and does not initiate connections to Redwood-managed control plane networks; only mTLS health pings are outbound to metrics.redwood.ai on port 443.

3) Logs & redaction: when you enable customer-managed logging, logs are written to your S3 bucket. We provide a processing pipeline that strips request bodies and PII fields before any telemetry leaves your bucket for our analytics (we document the exact fields in the compliance packet). See the CSV column 'log_handling' for the redaction policy.

Artifacts uploaded to your S3 path (signed URLs valid 7 days):
- s3://finpay-compliance/proof/priv-deploy-pt-summary-redacted.pdf
- s3://finpay-compliance/proof/vpc-segmentation-matrix.csv
- s3://finpay-compliance/proof/egress-acls.txt
- s3://finpay-compliance/proof/remediation-snapshots.zip

JIRA SUP-4982 (internal) contains the remediation runbook and verification steps; Nico can use the CloudTrail event above to validate the timestamped change. If you want, we can schedule a 20-minute evidence review with our security engineering team tomorrow.

Thanks — let me know if this completes FinPay's checklist.
